notice: Historical study compiled from public sources. Not a resume authored or endorsed by Grace Hopper. Confirmation records curator review, not subject verification.

profile.biography: Historical demonstration, not an account operated by Grace Hopper. Grace Hopper (1906–1992) studied mathematics and physics at Vassar and earned mathematics degrees at Yale. Her career included teaching, naval service and the computer industry. This selective study covers three milestones; it is not a complete biography. Dates use year precision. Skill labels are curator classifications. Confirmed means reviewed by the case curator, not verified by the subject.

project.title: A-0: automatic programming
project.background: Historical study of work on automatic programming. The learning category describes this curated study, not Hopper's employment status.

record.title: Developing A-0
record.result: An early step toward automatic programming.
record.validation: Yale's programming-pioneer section identifies the system and year; CHM describes her early compiler work. Curator review only.
record.remaining_work: The selected sources do not establish a benchmark, staffing count or detailed test procedure.

project.title: FLOW-MATIC: word-based programming
project.background: Historical study of making programming accessible through word-based commands.
project.team_outcome: Her team had FLOW-MATIC running in 1956.

record.title: Pursuing an English-word programming language
record.personal_action: Hopper pursued programming expressed in words; FLOW-MATIC was a team effort.
record.validation: Yale's biography supports the team milestone. Curator review only.
record.remaining_work: No claim is made that Hopper wrote every component alone.

project.title: COBOL: collaborative language development
project.background: Historical study of cooperation around a common business programming language.
project.team_outcome: COBOL emerged from contributions by multiple people.

record.title: Contributing to a shared business language
record.personal_action: Hopper participated in CODASYL in 1959 and supported COBOL's development and adoption.
record.validation: Yale and CHM describe her contribution. Curator review only.
record.remaining_work: These sources do not support sole authorship or modern cloud-platform experience.

excluded_topics: Awards are intentionally not imported; model memory is not an authorized portfolio source.
